sections.title: A varied genus
sections.text: Viburnum comprises woody shrubs and small trees native mainly to temperate and subtropical regions of the Northern Hemisphere, with species also reaching the Andes and tropical Asia. Leaf shape, flower-cluster structure and fruit colour differ among species; many have opposite simple leaves and small flowers in clusters.

sections.title: Flowers and fruits
sections.text: Viburnum fruits are fleshy drupes and may ripen red, black, blue or yellow; edibility and safety depend on the species, so the genus name alone is not enough to identify a safe food. The plate appears to depict V. opulus specifically: its palmately lobed leaves, flat flower clusters with enlarged marginal flowers, and red fruits are not representative of every Viburnum.
